key_insight: GridSFM uses a pretrained graph foundation model plus physics-informed fine-tuning to solve AC optimal power flow across many grid topologies and sizes, including unseen 10,000-bus systems.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable warm-start and surrogate strategy for power-system optimization that can reduce solver iterations and cost while generalizing beyond a single grid topology.
method: Pretrain a 15M-parameter physics-inspired GNN on 54 grid topologies with 500 to 4,000 buses.
Fine-tune on only 100 solved instances using Newton-method-informed physics constraints.
Handle disconnected AC-OPF feasible sets by lifting the problem with logarithmically penalized slacks and projecting back to feasibility.
evidence_signal: The model reports 2.45% zero-shot generation-cost error on a held-out 10,000-bus case and shows no degradation as system size increases, with improved warm-start performance versus dedicated single-topology neural networks.
watch_item: The approach depends on penalty design and projection back to the original feasible set, so robustness of those steps across diverse operating regimes should be validated carefully.
paper_title: GridSFM: A Foundation Model for Solving AC Optimal Power Flow
